reviews.text: Amazing!. Absolutely love this app. I’ve had it for years. Makes me feel good and motivated, and helps stretch me out and tone me up.💖

Not worth $50. I was charged $50 on day 6 when it was supposed to be a 7-day trial. I set a reminder to cancel it in time, but being charged early was not ok. The plan I chose has so little variety- first 4 days are the same, next ~7 are all the same, and so on. There is a HUGE skill jump from the easy level to medium level within the plan as well. When choosing between the different category tabs (strength, morning routine, etc.) the workouts are the same from one category to next, with very little variation. This app is NOT worth $50

I’ve found my favorites, but I wish there was a way to mark favorites, or at least see of history of what I’ve done so I can keep track of those favorites. Self-indulgent to the point of illogical. Terrible layout and nonsensical sessions. Each session is designated either “easy,” “medium,” or “hard.” The “easy” ones are ridiculously simple and could more be described as stretching as opposed to starting off with basic asanas. But then for some reason, an advanced asana is thrown right into the middle of all that less than basic stretching. 
Then after doing the exact same stretching for FOUR sessions, it moves the student on to the sessions deemed “medium,” which are anything but. These are four more sessions that are actually way more advanced asanas than what would be considered “medium,” and the instructors move quickly through them, which just makes no sense for someone having just learned stretches for the past four sessions. And yet again, highly advanced moves are thrown in as though the instructors just feel the need to show off their skills. I mean… The Crane… really??? 
The whole app has a very arrogant, self-congratulatory vibe to it, like someone was so impressed with their own yogi abilities they felt they just HAD to “teach” it… yet they do anything BUT actually teach yoga. Ridiculous app.

Great free content. What I really love about this app is that you get real, actual flows for free. I’ve tried lots of different yoga apps that give you a free trial for a day or a week but then make you pay to continue. I was so surprised to find that Sunsa Yoga is free and has so much content to choose from. Not only do you get daily flows, you can also choose from many options to work different parts of the body or different skills. While there’s not an option for personalized flows or other features you might find on subscription training apps, and most of the flows are rather repetitive, there is still so much more content than I expected for a free app. It has about the same if not more than some other apps that do require a subscription. Great app! Not great for beginners.... I have to commend this app for a variety of things. It has a great selection of classes to take and gives you your own customized plan all for free! However, the customized plans, or the one for me at the very least, is not very beginner friendly. The first group of classes was “easy” but included bridge pose and plow pose, which I would not consider beginner or easy poses by any means. Then it progresses into the next group of classes and it’s medium difficulty but includes crow and crane poses. After this group, it immediately progresses to hard classes with complicated poses. I want to improve my skills and I do appreciate them introducing more complex poses to us but I wish they would walk you through how to do the pose and progress up to it.

Great app but difficult for beginners to yoga. This app is great for guiding you through each pose with a clear demonstration and a calming voice over. I also like that it plays calming music in the background with a volume control separate to the coach’s voice, some apps I have used in the past don’t have this feature and won’t allow you to play your own music. 

I have tried to use other yoga apps in the past so have some experience of basic yoga moves and names. I feel that the guided workouts would be difficult without this knowledge and I would have to watch each video prior to the work out if I did not know the names of the moves. 

The personalised plan also seems good however the exercises progress very quickly into quite advanced stretches which are not suitable for beginners like me. Having said this there are lots of videos in the library to choose from which seem more my level.
